mainTopic: Watering fields and public work on חול המועד, and who wrote the משנה
overview: The משנה opens מסכת מועד קטן by allowing a person to water a thirsty field (בית השלחין) during חול המועד and שביעית, from a new spring or an old one. It forbids watering methods that take heavy effort, and it brings a מחלוקת about digging water channels. It ends with a list of public needs that may be taken care of on חול המועד. The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions the old spring at all. It answers that the type of spring does not matter: only a בית השלחין may be watered, and a rain-fed field (בית הבעל) may not. The גמרא then uses verses and their תרגום to show what the two field names mean. Next it asks which תנא wrote the משנה. רב הונא's answer, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, is rejected. רב פפא then names רבי יהודה, based on a ברייתא, which the גמרא explains. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to challenge רב פפא's proof, and the challenge continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Watering a thirsty field from any spring
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits watering a בית השלחין on חול המועד and in שביעית, from a new spring or an old one.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may water a field that needs watering during חול המועד and during שביעית, whether the water comes from a spring that just started flowing or from a spring that has been flowing for a long time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first rule: a field that depends on watering may be watered on חול המועד and in שביעית. It adds that the source of the water does not matter, new spring or old spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית השלחין will be badly damaged without water, so watering it counts as preventing a loss, which is allowed on חול המועד. The משנה mentions both kinds of springs, and that detail is exactly what the גמרא will ask about in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: A field that needs to be watered by hand because rain is not enough
Here: חול המועד, the in-between days of a יום טוב
The seventh year, when working the land is limited

phrases.english: One may water a field that needs irrigation
on חול המועד and during the seventh year,
both from a spring that has just started flowing,
and from a spring that did not just start flowing.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Watering a בית השלחין is permitted on חול המועד and in שביעית, from either a new or an old spring.

steps.title: Watering methods that are too much work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids watering with collected rainwater or with a קילון, and forbids making ditches around vines.
steps.simpleTranslation: But you may not water using rainwater, and not using water lifted up with a קילון. And you may not dig round ditches around grapevines.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now sets limits: some ways of watering, and some extra digging around vines, are not allowed on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Watering is allowed, but not by methods that need heavy effort, like drawing stored rainwater or lifting water up from a deep well with a lever. Digging ditches around vines is extra farm work beyond what is needed to prevent a loss, so it is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Rainwater, here meaning rainwater collected in a pit
A lever with a bucket used to lift water from a deep well
Round ditches dug around the base of a plant

phrases.english: But one may not water
neither with rainwater,
nor with water drawn by a קילון.
phrases.notes: A קילון is a long pole with a bucket on the end, used to lift water from deep down.

phrases.english: And one may not make round ditches for grapevines.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵין מַשְׁקִין לֹא מִמֵּי הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission given in step 1 by listing methods and work that are not allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Watering by heavy-effort methods (rainwater, קילון) and digging ditches around vines are forbidden on חול המועד.

steps.title: Disagreement about digging a new water channel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids digging a new אמה on חול המועד and in שביעית; the חכמים allow a new one in שביעית and only repairs on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: you may not dig a brand-new water channel on חול המועד or in שביעית. The חכמים say: you may dig a new channel in שביעית, and on חול המועד you may fix channels that got damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת about water channels. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is strict for both times, while the חכמים split the two times apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, digging a new channel is forbidden on חול המועד because it takes excessive effort. In שביעית, the concern is agricultural work: preparing the channel's banks for planting or appearing to hoe. The חכמים allow a new channel in שביעית, but on חול המועד allow only repairing an existing one.

keyTerms.meaning: A water channel or ditch that carries water to a field
From the start, here meaning brand new

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
One may not make a new water channel
on חול המועד or during the seventh year,
And the Sages say:
One may make a new water channel during the seventh year,
and one may repair damaged ones on חול המועד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from watering methods to digging the channels that bring the water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: no new אמה on חול המועד or in שביעית. חכמים: a new אמה is allowed in שביעית; on חול המועד only repairing damaged channels.

steps.title: Public works allowed on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists public needs that may be taken care of on חול המועד: water pits, roads, streets, מקוואות, marking graves, and uprooting כלאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may fix damaged water pits in public areas and clean them out. You may fix roads, streets and מקוואות, and do all the public's needs. You may mark graves, and inspectors may even go out to deal with כלאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns from a person's own field to the needs of the public, and lists jobs that may be done on חול המועד for everyone's benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the work was allowed to prevent a private loss. Here a new reason is added: work for צרכי רבים, public needs, is allowed too. Marking graves warns people about טומאה, and the inspectors deal with forbidden כלאים growing in fields.

keyTerms.meaning: Clean out by digging out the dirt
Pools of water, here meaning מקוואות for טבילה
Forbidden mixtures of plants growing together

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה allows two kinds of work on חול המועד: work to prevent a private loss (watering a needy field, repairing a channel) and work for the public's needs.

phrases.english: And one may repair damaged water places
phrases.notes: He means the public water pits and cisterns that people drink from.

phrases.english: that are in the public area,
and clean them out,
and one may repair the roads
and the streets and the pools of water,
and one may do all the public's needs,
and one may mark the graves,
and they may even go out about the כלאים.
phrases.notes: The inspectors go out to the fields to pull up כלאים that grew there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְתַקְּנִין אֶת קִלְקוּלֵי הַמַּיִם שֶׁבִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands from private field work to work done for the public.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Work for public needs, such as repairing water pits, roads and מקוואות, marking graves and handling כלאים, is permitted on חול המועד.

steps.title: Why mention the old spring at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the משנה permits even a new spring, which may collapse, why does it need to say an old, stable spring is permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now, if you can say that from a new spring, which might cave in, we may water, is it really necessary to say that from an old spring, which will not cave in, we may water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by questioning the wording of the משנה from step 1. It says the second half (the old spring) seems to be extra, since it is obviously allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new spring's walls are not yet firm and may collapse, which could lead to hard repair work, so it is the harder case to permit. If the משנה allows even that, then an old, stable spring is surely allowed. So the order 'new, and also old' looks backwards or needless, and the גמרא expects an answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is likely to fall in (collapse)
Is it necessary? (a way of saying 'this is obvious')

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether an old spring is allowed. Everyone agrees it is. The question is only why the משנה bothers to say it, after already permitting the harder case.

phrases.english: גמרא:
Now, if it can be said
that from a spring that just started flowing,
which is likely to collapse, one may water,
then from a spring that did not just start flowing,
which is not likely to collapse, is it necessary to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא יֵשׁ לוֹמַר מִמַּעְיָין שֶׁיָּצָא בַּתְּחִילָּה דְּאָתֵי לְאִינְּפוֹלֵי מַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first line of the משנה (step 1) and questions its wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's phrase 'בין ממעיין שלא יצא בתחילה' in step 1.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the harder case: if a new spring, which may collapse and cause extra work, is permitted, an old stable spring is surely permitted, so mentioning it seems needless.

steps.title: Both cases were needed: what we would have wrongly thought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה had to mention both springs. With only the new spring, we might have thought an old spring could water even a בית הבעל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: it was necessary. If the משנה had taught only a newly emerged spring, I would have said that only a בית השלחין may be watered from it, and a בית הבעל may not, because a new spring is likely to collapse. But an old spring is not likely to collapse, so I would have said that even a בית הבעל may be watered from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question from Step 5. It explains the mistake we would have made if the משנה had mentioned only the new spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with a new spring is that it may collapse, so using it takes a lot of effort. If the משנה had mentioned only the new spring, we might have thought that worry is the only reason a בית הבעל is excluded. Then an old, stable spring would seem allowed even for a בית הבעל.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary. Both cases in the משנה are needed.
I would have said. This introduces a wrong first assumption.
A field that rainwater is enough for
To collapse (the sides of a new spring caving in)

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only the 'wrong assumption' (הוה אמינא). It is not the final הלכה. The real conclusion comes in the next step.

phrases.english: They say: it was necessary.
phrases.notes: He means it was necessary for the משנה to mention both the new spring and the old spring.

phrases.english: If he had taught only a newly emerged spring,
I would have said:
here, it is a field that needs irrigation, yes,
a field that rain is enough for, no,
because it is likely to collapse.
But a spring that did not just emerge,
which is not likely to collapse,
I would say even a field that rain is enough for too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא from Step 5 by explaining why the old-spring case is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the new spring mentioned, we would think an old, stable spring may water even a בית הבעל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Given in Step 7: only a בית השלחין may be watered, from either kind of spring.

steps.title: The kind of spring does not matter; only the kind of field does
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that new and old springs are treated the same. A בית השלחין may be watered, and a בית הבעל may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us: there is no difference between a new spring and an old spring. A בית השלחין may be watered, and a בית הבעל may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer and gives the real lesson of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By mentioning the old spring too, the משנה shows that the deciding factor is the type of field, not how stable the spring is. Even from an easy, stable spring, a בית הבעל may not be watered on חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us. This introduces the real lesson.

steps.whatToRemember: On חול המועד, watering depends on the field. A בית השלחין (a field that needs water) may be watered from any spring. A בית הבעל (a rain-fed field) may not be watered, even from an old spring.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: the reason for allowing watering is the field's real need, not how easy the work is.

phrases.english: It teaches us:
there is no difference whether it is a newly emerged spring,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא מַעְיָין שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא בַּתְּחִילָּה,
phrases.english: or a spring that did not just emerge;

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין — אִין, בֵּית הַבַּעַל — לָא.
phrases.english: a field that needs irrigation, yes; a field that rain is enough for, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the wrong assumption from Step 6 and gives the final lesson.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The type of spring makes no difference. Only a בית השלחין may be watered on חול המועד.

steps.title: How do we know the name means a 'thirsty' field?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the term בית השלחין means a field that is thirsty.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that the term 'בית השלחין' is a word meaning thirst?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a word question: where does the name בית השלחין come from? It is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole rule depends on בית השלחין meaning a field that really needs water. So the גמרא wants a source showing that the word carries the idea of thirst.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is it implied? How do we know?

phrases.english: And from where is it implied that this term, 'a field that needs irrigation,'
is a term meaning thirst?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halacha to explaining the meaning of a key term in it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that בית השלחין means a thirsty field.

steps.title: Proof from the תרגום of 'faint and weary'
steps.stepSummary: The תרגום translates 'faint' as מְשַׁלְהֵי, which sounds like שלחין. So a בית השלחין is a 'thirsty' field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And you were faint and weary.' And we translate it: 'And you were thirsty (מְשַׁלְהֵי) and weary.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and its Aramaic translation, the תרגום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרגום uses the word מְשַׁלְהֵי for being worn out from thirst. That word is very close to שלחין. So בית השלחין means a field that is 'thirsty' and needs water.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (in a פסוק)
And we translate it (in the תרגום)

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And you were faint and weary,'
and we translate: 'And you were thirsty and weary.'
phrases.notes: Listen for the sound: מְשַׁלְהֵי is almost the same word as שלחין.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרגום renders 'faint' as מְשַׁלְהֵי (thirsty), which shows that שלחין means thirst.

steps.title: How do we know the name means a 'settled' field?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the term בית הבעל means a settled field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that the term 'בית הבעל' is a word meaning being settled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of word question about the second field name. It is setting up another proof from a תרגום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הבעל is a field that is already well taken care of by rain. The גמרא looks for a source showing that בעל carries the idea of being settled.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: being settled or established, not 'owner'

phrases.english: And from where is it implied that this term, 'a field that rain is enough for,'
is a term meaning being settled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as Step 8, now about the second term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that בית הבעל means a settled field.

steps.title: Proof from the תרגום of 'as a young man marries a maiden'
steps.stepSummary: The תרגום translates יִבְעַל as 'settles down'. So a בית הבעל is a settled field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'For as a young man marries (יִבְעַל) a maiden.' And we translate it: 'As a young man settles down with a maiden, so shall your sons settle within you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק and its תרגום, which shows that the root בעל means settling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרגום translates יִבְעַל with words for settling down. So בית הבעל means a field that is 'settled', meaning rain already supplies it. That is why it gets no permission to be watered on חול המועד.
steps.whatToRemember: בית השלחין is a 'thirsty' field (from מְשַׁלְהֵי), so it may be watered. בית הבעל is a 'settled' field (from מיתותב), so it may not.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'For as a young man marries a maiden,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: אֲרֵי כַּמָּה דְּמִיתּוֹתַב עוּלֵם עִם בְּתוּלְתָּא
phrases.english: and we translate: 'For just as a young man settles down with a maiden,'
phrases.notes: The key word is מיתותב, 'settles down'. It is how the תרגום renders יִבְעַל.

phrases.english: so shall your sons settle within you.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תרגום renders יִבְעַל as 'settles down', which shows that בעל means settled.

steps.title: Who is the author of our משנה's rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds two rules together: work to prevent a loss is allowed but work for profit is not, and even where there is a loss, heavy effort is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which תנא says that you may work to prevent a loss but not to make extra profit, and that even to prevent a loss you may not go to heavy effort?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking which named תנא holds the view of our unnamed משנה. This question sets up the rest of the section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה has two parts. A בית השלחין (thirsty field, a loss) may be watered, but a בית הבעל (rain-fed field, only profit) may not. The משנה also forbids hard methods of watering even for a thirsty field. The גמרא wants a תנא who holds both ideas.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period; here, the author of an unnamed משנה

steps.confusionAlert: There are TWO separate rules here: (1) profit is forbidden, and (2) heavy effort is forbidden even where there is a loss. The whole section depends on finding a תנא who holds BOTH.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna
[who holds] that [work to prevent] a loss — yes,
[work for] profit — no,
and even in a case of loss
we also do not go to heavy effort?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the terms of the משנה, the גמרא now looks for the משנה's author.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which named תנא holds both rules: loss yes and profit no, and no heavy effort even for a loss.

steps.title: רב הונא says it is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the author is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He allows drawing water from tree to tree but forbids watering the whole field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. As we learned: one may draw water from tree to tree, as long as he does not water the entire field.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a first answer and supports it with a משנה from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב allows small watering for each tree, which prevents a loss. He does not allow watering the whole field, since that is just extra profit. This matches the first rule of our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Provided that, only as long as

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.
As we learned in a mishna:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
One may draw water from tree to tree,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַשְׁקֶה אֶת הַשָּׂדֶה כּוּלָּהּ.
phrases.english: provided that he does not water the entire field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The author is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who forbids watering for profit (the whole field).

steps.title: That only covers profit, not effort where there is a loss
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: we only know that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב forbids work for profit. We never heard him forbid heavy effort where there is a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you heard that רבי אליעזר forbids work for profit. But did you ever hear him forbid heavy effort in a case of loss?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's answer because it only explains half of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's ruling matches the first rule (no profit). It says nothing about the second rule (no heavy effort even for a loss). So we cannot be sure he is the author of the whole משנה.

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Eliezer [hold]
phrases.notes: This is רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the last step, just called by a shorter name.

phrases.english: that [work for] profit is not [allowed];
[forbidding] effort in a case of loss —
did you hear him [say that]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's identification in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that רבי אליעזר בן יעקב is the author of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His source covers only the 'no profit' rule, not the 'no heavy effort even for a loss' rule.

steps.title: רב פפא says it is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא offers a new answer: the author is רבי יהודה. In a ברייתא about a new spring, רבי יהודה allows watering only a thirsty field that has dried up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יהודה. A ברייתא teaches: from a new spring, one may water even a rain-fed field. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: one may water only a thirsty field that dried up. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: neither this nor that.
steps.whatsHappening: Because רב הונא's answer fell short, רב פפא names a different תנא, רבי יהודה, and brings a ברייתא to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows even a בית הבעל, which is just for profit. רבי יהודה allows only a בית השלחין that dried up, which is a real loss. So רבי יהודה matches the 'loss yes, profit no' rule. The next line of the ברייתא will cover the effort rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A spring that comes out for the first time

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Pappa said:
Whose [view] is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda,
as it is taught in a baraita:
A spring that emerges for the first time —

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁקִין מִמֶּנּוּ אֲפִילּוּ שְׂדֵה בֵּית הַבַּעַל,
phrases.english: one may water from it even a rain-fed field,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מַשְׁקִין אֶלָּא שְׂדֵה בֵּית הַשְּׁלָחִין שֶׁחָרְבָה.
phrases.english: One may water only a thirsty field that has dried up.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
Neither this nor that.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָא מַנִּי — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב הונא's answer after the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the identification with a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The author was thought to be רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The author is רבי יהודה, who allows watering only a dried-up thirsty field.

steps.title: רבי יהודה also forbids redirecting a water channel
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that רבי יהודה goes further: a person may not redirect a water channel to water his garden or his ruined plot during חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, רבי יהודה said: A person may not redirect a water channel and water his garden or his ruined plot during חול המועד.
steps.whatsHappening: This last line of the ברייתא gives רבי יהודה's extra ruling about effort. It fills the gap that רב הונא's answer was missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redirecting a channel takes real work, so רבי יהודה forbids it even though the garden needs water. This matches the second rule of our משנה: no heavy effort even where there is a loss. Now רבי יהודה fits both halves of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The intermediate days of a festival (חול המועד)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's choice, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, covered only 'no profit.' רב פפא's choice, רבי יהודה, seems to cover both 'no profit' and 'no heavy effort even for a loss.' The גמרא challenges this proof in Step 20.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives רב פפא a source for the second rule of the משנה, no heavy effort even for a loss, which רב הונא's source lacked.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
A person may not redirect a water channel
and water his garden or his ruin
phrases.notes: A 'ruin' here is a ruined piece of land that is being used for planting.

phrases.english: during the intermediate days of a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא that רב פפא brought in step 15, covering the effort rule.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה forbids heavy effort even where there is a loss.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that one may not redirect a water channel during חול המועד.

steps.title: What does 'dried up' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה means by a 'dried up' field. If the field is already completely dead, watering it would do no good.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'dried up' mean? If you say the field is truly dried up, why would anyone need to water it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain a word in רבי יהודה's ruling from the ברייתא. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allowed watering a field that 'dried up.' But if the plants are already dead, watering cannot save anything, so the word cannot mean that. The גמרא needs a better meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (opening a possible reading that will be rejected)

phrases.english: What does "dried up" mean?
phrases.notes: This is the word from רבי יהודה's ruling in the ברייתא quoted in Step 15.

phrases.english: If you say it is literally dried up,
why do I need to water it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a key word in רבי יהודה's ruling from the ברייתא in Step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of 'חרבה' in רבי יהודה's ruling.

steps.title: אביי: the old spring dried up and a new one appeared
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'dried up' means the field's old water source ran dry, and a new spring appeared that can now water it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It means the field lost the water of its old spring, and a different spring came out for it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. The field itself is still alive, but its old spring has dried up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'dried up' part is the spring, not the plants. Without the new spring, the field will be ruined. So watering it during חול המועד prevents a real loss, and that is why רבי יהודה allows it.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That it dried up from this spring
and another spring came out for it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'חרבה' means the old spring dried up and a new spring appeared. The field needs the new water so it won't be ruined.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids a new spring in every case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view, and the גמרא explains it. A brand-new spring may never be used, whether or not the old spring dried up.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: neither this nor that. It makes no difference whether the field's spring dried up or did not dry up. A spring that has just come out may not be used.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next opinion in the same ברייתא. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה disagrees with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה allowed a new spring when the old one dried up. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה forbids a new spring in both situations. The words 'לא כך ולא כך' come from the ברייתא, and the 'לא שנא' line is the גמרא explaining what they mean.

keyTerms.meaning: a spring that has just come out for the first time

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
Neither this nor that,
phrases.notes: He means: not the thirsty field and not the dried-up field. Neither may be watered from a new spring.

phrases.english: it makes no difference whether its spring dried up
or whether its spring did not dry up
a newly emerged spring, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר לֹא כָּךְ וְלֹא כָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second, stricter opinion, and explains it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, a newly emerged spring may not be used for watering on חול המועד in any case.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה's limits apply only to a new spring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's proof. Maybe רבי יהודה allows a thirsty field and forbids a rain-watered field only when the water comes from a brand-new spring.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do you know? Perhaps רבי יהודה said 'a thirsty field, yes; a rain-watered field, no' only about a newly emerged spring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רבי יהודה really is the author of the משנה, as רב פפא claimed in Step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's limits in the ברייתא were stated about a brand-new spring, which is likely to collapse. Maybe that risk is his only reason for limiting watering to a בית השלחין. If so, he might allow even a בית הבעל from an old, stable spring. Our משנה forbids a בית הבעל from both kinds of spring (Step 7), so the ברייתא would not prove that רבי יהודה is its author.

keyTerms.meaning: he only said it here (and not in other cases)
a thirsty field that needs watering by hand
a field that gets enough water from rain

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying רבי יהודה disagrees with the משנה. It is only saying the proof from the ברייתא is not strong enough, because that case is limited to a new spring.

phrases.english: And from where do you know?

phrases.aramaic: דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Perhaps Rabbi Yehuda only said
a thirsty field, yes,
a rain-watered field, no,
only with a newly emerged spring

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof from the ברייתא that רב פפא used to show רבי יהודה is the author of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim in Step 15 that רבי יהודה is the author of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's 'בית השלחין yes, בית הבעל no' was said only about a new spring, which may collapse. From an old spring he might allow even a בית הבעל. That would go against the משנה, which forbids a בית הבעל from any spring (Step 7).
